Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the time to talk last week. HealthBridge is evaluating vendors for a patient-facing triage assistant and we need to confirm a few privacy points before we proceed with a formal RFP:

- Can Redwood sign a HIPAA BAA that covers PHI processing (patient identifiers, notes, and some uploaded documents)?
- For customers in our network who require US-only data residency, what are the options (hosted US-only, Dedicated, Private VPC, on-prem)?
- Who are the current subprocessors that touch data and which ones can be constrained to US-only?

I've attached a short vendor questionnaire and a reference architecture snapshot. Procurement would like a ballpark timeline for legal review and any gating items.

Hi Emily — great to hear from you and thanks for the questionnaire. Quick answers up front, then next steps:

1) BAA: Yes, Redwood can sign a HIPAA BAA. We keep an approved BAA template but legal occasionally requests a few carve-outs for on-prem requirements; we can share a draft next week.

2) Data residency options:
   - Hosted (Redwood API): data can be restricted to US cloud regions; for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private for stronger isolation.
   - Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with US-only tenancy; SLA-backed compute and retention controls.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): available for customers requiring full network isolation.

3) Subprocessors: we maintain a registry. Most subprocessors operate in US/EU regions; a subset (monitoring/telemetry vendors) are multi-region. We can provide a filtered list for US-only commitments and propose compensating controls where necessary.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll route the questionnaire and your residency ask to Legal + Platforms.
- Laura (cc'd) will validate subprocessor residency and highlight blockers for a US-only commitment.
- Marcus (cc'd) will provide a timeline and a preliminary commercial note (if you need a Dedicated estimate).

I'll attach our standard BAA draft once Legal and Platform have annotated the subprocessor matrix. Are you aiming for a contract by end of September? That helps prioritize the work.

Attachments: (none in this message)

Regards,

On Tue, Aug 11, 2026 at 10:08 AM soojin.lee@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi Emily — great to hear from you and thanks for the questionnaire. Quick answers up front, then next steps:

Thanks — adding technical detail here. Emily, tagging the short points that affect feasibility/cost:

- Subprocessor list: we'll export the current registry and mark which vendors are US-only. Expect telemetry/logging (vendor A) and error-monitoring (vendor B) to be multi-region today; we can run a remediation path but full US-only cutover is 6–8 weeks including contract changes.
- Dataflow: for PHI we recommend either Dedicated in a US region or Private VPC. Hosted US-only is workable but requires stronger contractual guarantees for retention and log access.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys in Private deployments; for Dedicated we provide region-restricted keys but not customer-managed HSM in the hosted tier.

Blockers to call out now:
1) Telemetry vendor contract clauses that prohibit residency restrictions — legal will need to negotiate.
2) If HealthBridge requires on-prem HSM for key custody, that pushes to Private on-prem and increases lead time.

I will attach the current subprocessor export and a short matrix mapping each subprocessors' region and purpose. Marcus — can you add a rough cost delta for Dedicated vs Private?

Attachments: dataflow-map.xlsx (XLSX), subprocessor-registry-export.csv (CSV)

Laura Bennett
